claims.text: The directory page bearing Lazar's name states its own scope, per Stanton Friedman, who obtained it: 'The page from the Los Alamos National Lab phone book with Lazar's name on it clearly states that it includes employees of the DOE and outside contractor, Kirk Meyer.' The company name is rendered 'Kirk Meyer' by Friedman and 'Kirk Mayer' or 'Kirk-Mayer' elsewhere; this node uses the kebab-case id kirk-mayer and records the spelling variance.

claims.source: Mark Farmer, recorded telephone interview, 25 May 1996, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/los-alamos-interview/ , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: A Los Alamos colleague of Lazar's, interviewed on tape by Mark Farmer on 25 May 1996 and anonymised at his own request, confirmed Lazar worked at the laboratory and said he 'was a contractor' under someone named Kirk Mayer.

Gene Huff, writing in Lazar's defence rather than against him, records that Kirk-Mayer issued Lazar a 'Z number' of 094729 on 18 May 1982, and that both Los Alamos National Laboratory and Kirk-Mayer subsequently said they held no employment records for him.

Tom Mahood's 2018 conclusion on the same question: that Lazar worked as an electronic technician for Kirk-Mayer, a contractor supplying support staff, rather than as a physicist, and that his presence in the telephone directory reflected that contractor relationship and was marked with a 'K/M' notation.

desc: The smallest node in this cluster and possibly the most useful, because it converts a disputed sentence into a precise one. 'Lazar worked at Los Alamos' has been argued about for thirty-five years. 'Lazar worked at Los Alamos as a contract technician for Kirk-Mayer' is what the opened record actually supports, and it is supported from three directions that do not share a source: the telephone directory page carrying his name states on its face that it covers Department of Energy employees and the outside contractor Kirk-Mayer; a Los Alamos colleague interviewed on tape in 1996 said Lazar 'was a contractor' under Kirk Mayer; and Gene Huff, writing in Lazar's defence, records a Kirk-Mayer employee number issued on 18 May 1982. The node also does work the board needs beyond this cluster: it is a named support contractor at a national laboratory, which is the contractor spine the board's own gap list has been asking for, and it joins lanl, l-los-alamos, doe and d-contractor.
